name: Dense Granule Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Platelet Dense Granule Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Absence or marked reduction of dense granules in platelets on electron microscopy
Clinical history of mucocutaneous bleeding such as easy bruising, epistaxis, or menorrhagia
Abnormal platelet aggregation response to ADP and epinephrine with normal platelet count
Exclusion of other inherited or acquired platelet function disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent or markedly reduced dense granules on electron microscopy plus clinical bleeding symptoms and abnormal platelet aggregation testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not always available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked reduction or absence of platelet dense granules

pathognomonic.notes: Includes easy bruising, epistaxis, and menorrhagia
searchTerms: tendency to bleed from skin and mucous membranes
bleeding from mucous surfaces and skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal platelet aggregation response to ADP and epinephrine
searchTerms: poor platelet response to ADP and adrenaline
bleeding lasts long after small cuts

laboratory: Normal platelet count with abnormal platelet function tests
Absent or decreased dense granules on platelet electron microscopy
imaging: Electron microscopy of platelets showing absent dense bodies
genetic: Mutations in genes involved in dense granule biogenesis (e.g., HPS genes in Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome variants)
other: Normal platelet morphology on light microscopy

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of alpha granules instead of dense granules
Large, gray-appearing platelets on blood smear
Defect in platelet adhesion due to GPIb deficiency

redFlags: Severe mucocutaneous bleeding disproportionate to platelet count
Bleeding complications following surgery or trauma
Intracranial hemorrhage or other life-threatening bleeding events
references: Nurden AT. Platelets, Dense Granules and Dense Granule Deficiency. Platelets. 2011;22(7):515-522.
Savoia A, et al. Platelet Dense Granule Deficiency: Clinical and Laboratory Features. Haematologica. 2000;85(10):1024-1030.
